name: ccp3.dfgateway.com
body: Every page has a title, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds.
lesson: Keep body text at a 4.5:1 contrast ratio or more against its background.
summary: The site's bot protection refused the plain request; the page was analyzed in headless Chrome. Partial analysis: 2 of 2 linked pages answered with a bot check or a block, so the scores rest mostly on the start page. ccp3.dfgateway.com scores 63 out of 100 (D). 5 checks fail now, 27 are at risk, and 22 pass. Fix first: elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds.

fix.title: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
fix.evidence: axe-core 4.14.0 found 11 elements on /cm/, for example .i-already-have-an-ac > a and .login_terms > .legal-here-dolor-sit > .green-color[href$="terms-conditions"]. Impact: serious.
fix.fix: Darken the text or lighten the background until normal text reaches 4.5:1 and large text 3:1.

fix.title: 3 form controls have no label
fix.evidence: On /cm/. Screen readers announce them as an unnamed field.
fix.fix: Pair each control with <label for>, wrap it in a label, or add aria-label.

fix.title: Tracking starts on load and no banner asks first
fix.evidence: No cookie banner appeared. Before any choice, Chromium from an EU address (Belgium) saw Google Analytics (2 requests), Hotjar (1 request), and cookies _ga_T4L3F5VF9M, _ga, _ga_NPV1G8KWT9, _hjSessionUser_3251825, _hjSession_3251825.
fix.fix: Hold every tag until consent, or set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads. Block third-party embeds until the visitor agrees.

fix.title: Tracking tags load with no consent tool in the page
fix.evidence: Google Analytics 4, Hotjar appear in the HTML and no consent platform or Google Consent Mode default was found. In the EU, the UK, Brazil, and Colombia this is a legal exposure.
fix.fix: Add a consent platform and set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads.

fix.title: The start page took 3662 ms to arrive
fix.evidence: That is the HTML alone, before images and scripts.
fix.fix: Cache the HTML at the edge, or speed up the server render.

fix.title: Core Web Vitals fail for real visitors
fix.evidence: Real Chrome users over the last 28 days on this page, at the 75th percentile: Largest Contentful Paint 5.2 s (poor), Interaction to Next Paint 199 ms (good), Cumulative Layout Shift 0.2 (needs improvement). Source: Chrome UX Report through PageSpeed Insights.
fix.fix: Make the largest element arrive sooner: preload the hero image, serve it at the shown size in a modern format, and cut render-blocking scripts. Reserve space for images, embeds, ads, and late banners.

works.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
Plain http does not serve the site
Every image has an alt attribute
The largest element paints in 1.8 s
The start page sets a mobile viewport
